name: Developing POC Ratchet
note: Builds the DEVELOPING volume-at-price profile inside each RTH session, rows 0.05 daily ATR wide, and records the developing point of control at every 30-minute period close. Goes long when the POC has ratcheted monotonically up for `runs` consecutive periods, has travelled at least mig*ATRd in total (strict=1 additionally demands a move in every single period, which real developing POCs rarely deliver), has never printed below the base of the ratchet at any earlier period today, and price is above it; short is the exact mirror. One entry per session, none before 11:00 or after 14:00 ET. The exit is the idea's other half: the stop starts at the base of the ratchet and then TRAILS ON THE DEVELOPING POC ITSELF, checked only at period closes, flat by 15:55. The session clock is derived with utc_offset (4 = EDT; set 5 for winter data).
source: Developing POC / developing value area is standard Market Profile instrumentation (Steidlmayer, CBOT Market Profile; Dalton et al., 'Mind Over Markets'), and Sierra Chart documents 'Volume Point Of Control For Bars' and developing value-area studies as built-in tools. The monotone-ratchet predicate, the migration-distance gate and the POC-trailing exit are the harvester's quantification (synthesis).
code:
def family_init(ctx):
    b = ctx.bars
    n = len(b)
    h = [float(x["h"]) for x in b]
    l = [float(x["l"]) for x in b]
    c = [float(x["c"]) for x in b]
    v = [float(x.get("v") or 0.0) for x in b]

    off = int(ctx.p.utc_offset) * 60
    rs = int(ctx.p.rth_start)
    re_ = int(ctx.p.rth_end)
    pl = int(ctx.p.period_min)

    etm = [0] * n
    day = [None] * n
    for j in range(n):
        s = str(b[j]["t"])
        day[j] = s[:10]
        etm[j] = int(s[11:13]) * 60 + int(s[14:16]) - off

    # bar length in minutes, from the data itself
    barm = None
    for j in range(1, min(n, 400)):
        d = etm[j] - etm[j - 1]
        if d > 0 and (barm is None or d < barm):
            barm = d
    if not barm:
        barm = pl

    sessno = [0] * n
    per = [None] * n
    inrth = [0] * n
    pend = [0] * n
    cur = None
    sn = -1
    for j in range(n):
        if day[j] != cur:
            cur = day[j]
            sn += 1
        sessno[j] = sn
        if rs <= etm[j] < re_:
            inrth[j] = 1
            per[j] = (etm[j] - rs) // pl
            if barm >= pl:
                pend[j] = 1
            elif ((etm[j] - rs) % pl) + barm >= pl:
                pend[j] = 1
    nsess = sn + 1
    npers = (re_ - rs + pl - 1) // pl

    # daily ATR, from completed RTH sessions only
    shi = [None] * nsess
    slo = [None] * nsess
    scl = [None] * nsess
    for j in range(n):
        if not inrth[j]:
            continue
        s = sessno[j]
        shi[s] = h[j] if shi[s] is None else max(shi[s], h[j])
        slo[s] = l[j] if slo[s] is None else min(slo[s], l[j])
        scl[s] = c[j]
    tr = [None] * nsess
    for s in range(nsess):
        if shi[s] is None:
            continue
        pc = scl[s - 1] if s > 0 else None
        if pc is None:
            tr[s] = shi[s] - slo[s]
        else:
            tr[s] = max(shi[s] - slo[s], abs(shi[s] - pc), abs(slo[s] - pc))
    ad = int(ctx.p.atr_days)
    atrd = [None] * nsess
    for s in range(nsess):
        seg = [tr[q] for q in range(max(0, s - ad), s) if tr[q] is not None]
        if len(seg) >= max(3, ad // 2):
            atrd[s] = sum(seg) / len(seg)

    # developing volume-at-price profile, rebuilt each session from 09:30
    pocs = [[None] * npers for _ in range(nsess)]
    prof = {}
    wrow = None
    cs = -1
    for j in range(n):
        if not inrth[j]:
            continue
        s = sessno[j]
        if s != cs:
            cs = s
            prof = {}
            wrow = None
            a = atrd[s]
            if a and a > 0:
                wrow = float(ctx.p.row_w) * a
        if not wrow or wrow <= 0:
            continue
        r0 = int(l[j] / wrow)
        r1 = int(h[j] / wrow)
        if r1 < r0:
            r1 = r0
        nr = r1 - r0 + 1
        if nr > 400:
            nr = 400
            r1 = r0 + 399
        share = v[j] / nr
        for r in range(r0, r1 + 1):
            prof[r] = prof.get(r, 0.0) + share
        if pend[j]:
            bestr = None
            bestv = -1.0
            for r, vv in prof.items():
                if vv > bestv:
                    bestv = vv
                    bestr = r
            if bestr is not None:
                pocs[s][per[j]] = (bestr + 0.5) * wrow

    runs = int(ctx.p.runs)
    ep = int(ctx.p.early_p)
    lp = int(ctx.p.late_p)
    mig = float(ctx.p.mig)
    sig = [0] * n
    taken = set()
    for j in range(n):
        if not inrth[j] or not pend[j]:
            continue
        s = sessno[j]
        p = per[j]
        if s in taken or p < max(ep, runs - 1) or p > lp:
            continue
        a = atrd[s]
        if not a or a <= 0:
            continue
        arr = pocs[s]
        seq = arr[p - runs + 1:p + 1]
        if len(seq) < runs or any(x is None for x in seq):
            continue
        base = seq[0]
        hist = [x for x in arr[:p + 1] if x is not None]
        if int(ctx.p.strict):
            up = all(seq[q + 1] > seq[q] for q in range(runs - 1))
            dn = all(seq[q + 1] < seq[q] for q in range(runs - 1))
        else:
            # a ratchet is a mode that never steps BACK; requiring it to move
            # in every single period is a stronger claim than the idea makes,
            # so the net migration gate below carries the "it moved" part
            up = (all(seq[q + 1] >= seq[q] for q in range(runs - 1))
                  and seq[-1] > seq[0])
            dn = (all(seq[q + 1] <= seq[q] for q in range(runs - 1))
                  and seq[-1] < seq[0])
        if up and (seq[-1] - base) >= mig * a and min(hist) >= base and c[j] > seq[-1]:
            sig[j] = 1
            taken.add(s)
        elif dn and (base - seq[-1]) >= mig * a and max(hist) <= base and c[j] < seq[-1]:
            sig[j] = -1
            taken.add(s)

    ctx.sig = ctx.series(sig, "poc_ratchet")
    ctx._atrd = atrd
    ctx.pocs = pocs
    ctx.sessno = sessno
    ctx.per = per
    ctx.pend = pend
    ctx.inrth = inrth
    ctx.etm = etm


def signal(ctx, i):
    s = ctx.sig[i]
    return 0 if s is None else int(s)


def exit_signal(ctx, i):
    if not ctx.positions:
        return False
    e = ctx.positions[0]["entry_i"]
    if ctx.sessno[i] != ctx.sessno[e]:
        return True
    if not ctx.inrth[i] or ctx.etm[i] >= int(ctx.p.flat_min):
        return True
    if not ctx.pend[i]:
        return False
    p = ctx.per[i]
    pe = ctx.per[e]
    if p is None or pe is None:
        return True
    arr = ctx.pocs[ctx.sessno[i]]
    runs = int(ctx.p.runs)
    q0 = pe - runs + 1
    if q0 < 0:
        q0 = 0
    stop = arr[q0]
    if stop is None:
        return True
    long_ = ctx.positions[0]["side"] == "long"
    # trail the stop on the developing POC itself, one completed period behind
    for q in range(pe, p):
        val = arr[q]
        if val is None:
            continue
        if long_ and val > stop:
            stop = val
        elif (not long_) and val < stop:
            stop = val
    px = ctx.c[i]
    return px < stop if long_ else px > stop
